items.title: Two charged, one suspect wanted after Mississauga apartment arsons
items.summary: Two people have been charged and a third suspect is wanted following two fires at a Mississauga apartment building that caused an estimated $1 million in damage earlier this year. In a news release, Peel police say the fires were deliberately set in a third-floor hallway of the building near Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road on Sept. 20 and 21. Investigators believe occupants of one of the units were deliberately targeted in both incidents. No significant injuries were reported, several residents were displaced in addition to a large-scale evacuation. Officials say 18 residents were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation. As part of the investigation, police identified three people believed to be involved. Joshua Pedersen, 28, of no fixed address, was arrested in Hamilton on Oct. 15 and charged with two counts of arson – disregard for human life, two counts of mischief over $5,000, break and enter with intent to commit an indictable offence and possession of break-in instruments. Meanwhile, 27-year-old Morgan Murphy, of Burlington, was arrested on Oct. 26 and charged with two counts each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence and arson – disregard for human life. Both accused were held in custody pending bail hearings.

items.title: Two charged in arson investigation at Mississauga apartment building; third suspect sought
items.summary: Two people face charges and a third person is sought in an arson investigation at a Mississauga apartment building. Emergency crews responded to fires in a third-floor hallway of an apartment building in the area of Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road in Clarkson on Sunday, Sept. 20, and Monday, Sept. 21, Peel Regional Police said. Police said the fires were deliberately set in the hallway, and investigators believe the occupants of one unit were deliberately targeted in both fires. No significant injuries were reported in either incident, police said. However, the second fire resulted in a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents, police added. Police said 18 residents were transported to hospital for treatment of smoke inhalation. The estimated damage is approximately $1 million. Police made two arrests and are searching for an additional suspect in connection with the investigation.

items.title: Mississauga certified election results show Tedjo winning all but 1 ward — here’s how the mayoral vote broke down
items.summary: Tedjo’s vote share grew across every ward compared to the 2024 byelection. Alvin Tedjo celebrates with supporters on election night after winning the Mississauga mayoral race with 74,479 votes. Mississauga’s mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo won 10 of 11 wards, an analysis of certified election results by Mississauga News shows. The only ward he lost was to the runner-up — incumbent and now outgoing mayor Carolyn Parrish, who finished ahead in Ward 5. The other two high-profile challengers — former mayor Bonnie Crombie and Coun. Dipika Damerla — did not win any ward. Certified results showed that while 191,166 cast a ballot in the Oct. 26 municipal election, 1,212 didn’t cast a vote for mayor. Total ballots cast for mayor were 189,954. items.title: Be aware of fraudulent QR codes on parking machines in Mississauga
items.summary: Reminder to all residents and visitors that QR code stickers posted on parking machines are never used to collect payment for parking in the city. Emergency and public safety | November 5, 2026 On November 4, the City became aware of fraudulent QR code stickers placed on parking Pay and Display machines across the city. City staff were deployed immediately and removed these stickers from parking machines. These unauthorized QR codes are designed to redirect users to third-party payment sites that are not affiliated with the City. Scanning and using these codes put your personal and financial information at risk. The City wants to reassure residents that City staff continue to monitor parking machines and equipment and respond quickly to reports. In Mississauga, QR code stickers posted on parking machines are never used to collect payment for parking. Parking and payment instructions can be found on the parking machine digital screen or on surrounding official City signage. The only way to pay for City parking is through parking machines using the digital payment prompts, where certain payment options are accepted like coins, payment apps like Apple Pay or Google Wallet or major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) at all locations. PayByPhone is also available in Streetsville. Any QR code found on a City paid parking machine is not legitimate and should not be scanned. Fraudulent QR code stickers are often placed over existing signage or payment instructions and can redirect users to fake payment websites that look legitimate but are designed to steal personal and financial information.

items.title: Massive 176,000-Square-Foot Grocery Store Opens in Mississauga with Global Food as Its Draw
items.summary: Food World Plus, described as Ontario's largest grocery store, opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East in Mississauga. According to the store, its 176,000-square-foot facility is built around global food, offering products and ingredients from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. The store said it aims to give shoppers in Mississauga's diverse community access to ingredients they might otherwise need to visit several specialty grocers to find. Beyond its international aisles, Food World Plus is positioning itself as a one-stop destination with a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and in-house butcher. The store said its meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards from delivery through to the cuts prepared for customers. Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford and later welcomed the new store to the city in a social media post.

items.title: Mississauga Inclusive-Leadership Expert Named Finalist for Speaker Slam's Top Honour
items.summary: Karen Craggs, a Mississauga-based inclusive leadership expert and keynote speaker, is one of 14 finalists competing for Speaker Slam's Inspirational Speaker of the Year title on Nov. 21. According to organizers, the Toronto-based competition draws entries from qualifying tournaments held across North America throughout the year, with the strongest speakers advancing to the Grand Slam Inspirational Speaking Final at CBC's Glenn Gould Studio. Organizers said this year's finals mark the 10th annual edition of what they describe as North America's largest competition of its kind. The winner will receive $5,000 in cash along with a prize package valued at up to $50,000, organizers said. Speaker Slam co-founder Dan Shaikh said in a news release that this year's theme, built around the idea of a catalyst and how change shapes a person into someone who changes things for others, describes Craggs' life's work. Shaikh noted that Craggs is well known for championing inclusive leadership, a management style focused on valuing and empowering diverse team members.

items.title: Streetsville Councillor Says New Operator May Be Lined Up for Shuttered Franklin House
items.summary: The Franklin House, a longtime restaurant and bar in one of Mississauga's most historic buildings, is currently closed, leaving residents in Streetsville wondering what comes next for the landmark. According to Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt, he has heard a new operator may be preparing to take over the business and could reopen it soon. Butt said he has not been contacted directly by anyone involved in the business and does not know whether a new operator would keep the Franklin House name or its current restaurant format. He said it remains unclear whether the space would continue to run as it has, or shift to a different format. Butt also pointed to challenges that come with operating in the historic building, including a relatively small main-floor dining area and limited space upstairs. He said the upper floor is better suited to occasional private functions than regular restaurant service, while the basement presents another challenge due to flooding risk.

A Mississauga man who has been playing the lottery regularly for about a decade has won his first major prize. Corey John won an Encore prize of $100,000 in the Sept. 19 Lotto 6-49 draw. “My biggest win before this was $500,” he said in an Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corp. news release. ” He said when he shared the news with his fiancée, she didn’t believe him at first. “I think a vacation is coming up. Maybe a little renovation to the house too,” he said of his plans for the winnings. The winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada gas station on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga.

items.title: Mississauga Man's Decade of Steady Lotto Play Pays Off with $100,000 Encore Win
items.summary: Corey John, a Mississauga man who has played the lottery regularly with OLG for about a decade, is $100,000 richer after his Sept. 19 Lotto 6/49 ticket matched six of seven Encore numbers in exact order. According to the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation, the winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada gas station on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga. John told OLG officials his previous biggest win was $500, calling that one exciting but saying this win is a little more exciting. He said the moment he found out was completely unexpected, and that his fiancee didn't believe him at first when he told her the news. John, who plays Lotto 6/49 twice weekly and always adds Encore, picked up his cheque at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto. He said he has plans for the windfall, including a vacation and possibly a renovation to his house.
